themes_detail.label: Street Light Outages Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street lighting failures in Morningside Heights spiked to 32 complaints two weeks ago—a 422% increase from the 6.1-complaint weekly baseline—suggesting a possible infrastructure failure or maintenance gap affecting public safety and visibility across the district.
evidence: 32 street light complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 6.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 12.39)
422% spike—highest statistical anomaly in the dataset
Aligns with community board's repeated requests for transit/infrastructure capital funding
reporting_angles: Contact DOT to determine if a specific equipment failure, contractor issue, or maintenance backlog triggered the outages
Interview residents about safety concerns from darkened streets; check crime/incident reports correlated with outage timeline

themes_detail.label: Illegal Street Vending Crackdown
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints exploded to 13 this week, up 846% from the 1.4-complaint weekly average, indicating either a new enforcement initiative or a sudden surge in unpermitted vending that triggered city response.
evidence: 13 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average (z-score: 11.72)
Potential connection to ongoing ULURP development activity at 1727 Amsterdam Avenue or neighborhood activation
reporting_angles: Contact local precinct and DOE Vending Unit to confirm if a new enforcement sweep was launched; ask about its scope and duration
Interview street vendors and local business owners about enforcement activity and how it's affecting the informal economy

themes_detail.label: Water Quality Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Water quality complaints tripled to 3 complaints two weeks ago from a near-zero baseline of 0.4 weekly average, signaling potential contamination, discoloration, or service disruptions affecting drinking water or pipes in the district.
evidence: 3 water quality complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.42, 700% spike)
Baseline was already very low, suggesting even small volume represents unusual departure
Aligns with chronic heat/hot water issues (3,105 complaints over 90 days) hinting at broader plumbing/water infrastructure stress
reporting_angles: Contact NYC DEP to check for water main breaks, treatment alerts, or boil notices issued in Morningside Heights 2 weeks ago
Interview residents about water discoloration, taste, or odor incidents; cross-check with local social media or neighborhood apps

themes_detail.label: Homeless Assistance Requests Rise
themes_detail.summary: Homeless person assistance complaints jumped to 14 two weeks ago, a 387% spike from the 2.9-complaint weekly baseline, indicating either an increase in street homelessness or an emerging encampment requiring city intervention.
evidence: 14 homeless person assistance complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.9 weekly average (z-score: 4.6, 387% spike)
Aligns with community board's repeated budget requests for 'outreach services to homebound older adults' suggesting ongoing service gap
Non-Emergency Police Matter complaints also up 220% last week (8 vs. 2.5 avg), suggesting broader social disorder
reporting_angles: Contact DOHMH and Department of Social Services to identify if a new encampment emerged, or if an existing service closure redirected clients to Morningside Heights
Interview homeless services providers and community advocates about whether district is becoming a new hub; document specific locations and conditions

themes_detail.label: Graffiti and Overgrown Tree Issues
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti and overgrown tree complaints both spiked 300–700% over the past 3 weeks (3 complaints each vs. 0.8 and 0.4 weekly baselines), suggesting deteriorating public realm maintenance or a coordinated environment neglect affecting neighborhood aesthetics.
evidence: Graffiti: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 3.4, 300% spike)
Overgrown Tree/Branches: 3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 3.77, 700% spike)
Both suggest contractor or city maintenance gap; may indicate resource reallocation or service backlog post-pandemic
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks and Sanitation to determine if graffiti removal or tree maintenance crews were reassigned or reduced
Walk the district to map affected streets and assess whether complaints cluster geographically; interview residents about visible decay
